name: self-remote-control
description: Lets a session report on its own Remote Control, turn it on under a title, and rename itself. After a login change it reconnects Remote Control and resumes a turn the change cut off. It runs /remote-control only when the session reads as not connected, so it never opens the Remote Control panel or disconnects.

reconnectOnLoginChange.title: Reconnect after a login change
reconnectOnLoginChange.description: When the account this machine is signed in as changes (a /login, or a tool swapping the stored login), run /remote-control again under the session's title if Remote Control was connected before the change or the Remote Control for all sessions setting is on. It runs only while the session reads as not connected, never while connected.

resumeAfterLoginChange.title: Resume after a login change
resumeAfterLoginChange.description: When the account changes and this session's last turn ended, within 6 hours, on an error a new login can clear (the usage limit, a failed sign-in), send it: There was a small interruption. Please resume from your last turn normally. Once per change, after the Remote Control reconnect and a delay of up to a minute, never to a session at a finished break, and not again after a resume that failed at once until you type.

updateCheck.title: Update check
updateCheck.description: on: when a tool of this plugin is called and the last check is 30 minutes old, fetch this plugin's published plugin.json from GitHub (a plain GET of a public file) and say when a newer version is out. off: never check.
